{
  "B_expression": "-1/(8*(1+u)**3) + (r*(sqrt(1+r)+3))/(8*(1+sqrt(1+r))**3)",
  "C_expression": "-1/(2*(1+u))",
  "derivation": "Retain the source quadratic correction but add a smooth cross-term and a u-dependent bridge in the r^2 coefficient. Let q=1+u and s=sqrt(1+r). The source body B0=-1/(2*(1+s)**2) gives g0=r/2+r^2*B0=s-1, so the pure remainder 2g+g^2-r is zero when u=0. The whole residual is E=2*q*g+g^2-r. The exact positive-branch increment is sqrt(q^2+r)-q = r/(2*q)-r^2/(8*q^3)+O(r^3). Set C=-1/(2*q), so r/2+u*r*C = r/(2*q) exactly. For the r^2 coefficient, use B=-1/(8*q^3)+(B0+1/8). Since B0+1/8 = r*(s+3)/(8*(1+s)**3), B is smooth and equals B0 at u=0. Thus g = r/(2*q)-r^2/(8*q^3)+r^2*(B0+1/8), matching the exact increment through O(r^2), preserving the exact u=0 source cancellation, and leaving only O(u*r^3+r^4) local coefficient error. This is a local coefficient-family improvement for the two-slot quotient, not a full NS/PDE certificate. Both bodies are smooth on a neighborhood of |r|<=1/2, |u|<=1/4 because 1+r>0 and 1+u>0 there.",
  "inspect": [],
  "note": "Successor should check that (1) ZERO and u=0 rows remain exactly unchanged in the pure remainder; (2) rows with small nonzero u and |r|<1/4 now have cross residual reduced from O(u*r) toward O(u*r^3) in the inner chi-supported region; (3) rows with |u|>=1/4 still fall outside chi_u support and receive only the r/2 step; (4) the analytic domain is local (r>-1, u>-1), with the outer rectangle safely inside, and no full PDE certificate is claimed; (5) finite numeric residuals are not a proof of smoothness, but the elementary functions give an open-neighborhood smooth family."
}
